title: Saint Genevieve where he had read, sheltered from the sin of Paris,
html_source: Saint Genevieve is the patron saint of Paris the city, offering up multiple ways to interpret the “sin of Paris,” which on the one hand could refer to Paris’s sin in judging in favor of Aphrodite over Hera and Athena, or his sin in kidnapping Helen of Troy. Another reading suggests that hiding and reading in the library of Saint Genevieve, night after night, he does not succumb to the debauchery of the city of lights. Of course, it’s unclear to whom Joyce is referring when he uses the pronoun ‘he’ (Stephen? Aristotle?).
